simple.meaning: חָסַד (châçad) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, perhaps to bow (the neck only [compare 2603 ] in courtesy to an equal), i.e. to be kind ; also (by euphemistically [compare 1288 ], but rarely) to reprove.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חָסַד (H2616) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Samuel 22:26, with occurrences in 2 Samuel, Psalms, Proverbs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָסַד (H2616) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חָסַד (H2616) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חָסַד (châçad) / H2616 is traced through 2 Samuel 22:26, Psalms 18:26, Proverbs 25:10 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H2616. chacad I. [ חָסַד ] verb 1. be good, kind (Late Hebrew חָסַד in derivatives חָסִיד pious ; Aramaic חֲסַד be kind, mild (then beg ), chiefly in derivatives חִסְדָּא etc.; compare perhaps Arabic usually plural they assembled , followed by they combined for him, and took pains to shew him courtesy Lane 574c , also RS Proph. iv. n. 9 (and Schu AE see in Thes); > Thes and others Find primary meaning in eager zeal or desire (|| קנא ), whence develop kindness (as above), and envy , Arabic , envy (verb & noun), Aramaic חֲסַד be put to shame , , חַסֵּד reproach, revile , v, II. חסד ) — only Hithpa`el Imperfect תִּתְחַסָּ֑ד עִםחָֿסִיד thou shewest thyself kind 2Sam 22:26 = Psa 18:26 . — On Pi`el Prov 25:10 see II. חסד . II. [ חָסַד ] verb be reproached, ashamed (Aramaism, see RS Proph. iv, n. 9 ; Aramaic חֲסַד be put to shame , , חַסֵּד reproach, revile ; חִסּוּדָא , shame, reproach , often in ᵐ5 ᵑ7 for חֶרְמָּה ); — only Pi`el Imperfect מֶּןיְֿחַסֶּדְךָ Prov 25:10 lest he reproach thee, expose thee to shame.
